items.bodyExcerpt:
# **问题背景**

为聚焦资源保障 PyTorch 后端的持续演进，MindSpeed 套件已正式启动 **MindSpore 后端"日落计划"**：停止 MindSpore 框架后端的开发与支持，MindSpeed-LLM 仓库将移除 MindSpore 相关代码、文档、示例与测试。

**此举措旨在：**

- 聚焦维护精力：将有限的社区维护资源集中在活跃度更高的 PyTorch 后端上。
- 降低使用成本：避免用户在两套后端间选择与适配时产生额外负担。
- 保持仓库健康：移除已停止演进的适配层，减少存量代码的维护与门禁成本。

我们称此计划为"日落计划"，象征着对完成使命的 MindSpore 后端致以谢意并优雅地告别。

# **主要举措**

- 删除 `docs/zh/mindspore`、`docs/en/mindspore`（MindSpore 安装/快速入门/支持模型文档）
- 删除 `examples/mindspore`（llama2 / llama3 / glm4 / deepseek2 / deepseek3 / qwen 系列 / qwen3_moe 等 MindSpore 训练与转换示例）
- 删除 `mindspeed_llm/mindspore`（MindSpore 后端适配包）与 `tests/mindspore`（0day / ST 测试）
- 删除 `mindspeed_llm/features_manager/ai_framework`（`--ai-framework mindspore` 特性注册）与 `ci/access_control_test_ms.py`
- `rlhf_gpt.py`：移除 MindSpore 分支，RLHF 固定使用默认 `RayActorGroup` launcher
- `README.md` / `README_en.md` 移除 MindSpore 支持公告条目

**对应变更 MR**：https://gitcode.com/Ascend/MindSpeed-LLM/merge_requests/5058

# **影响说明**

- `--ai-framework mindspore` 参数不再支持，MindSpore 后端文档、示例与测试一并移除
- **PyTorch 后端完全不受影响**，pretrain / finetune / RLHF 各入口用法不变
- 套件内其他仓库同步日落：MindSpeed（!3993）、MindSpeed-MM（!3159，公告 issue [#717](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/MindSpeed-MM/issues/717)）、MindSpeed-Core-MS（!764）

# **用户指引**

如您仍在使用 MindSpeed-LLM 的 MindSpore 后端，请在本 issue 下留言说明使用场景，我们将评估并协助迁移；对 PyTorch 后端的使用无任何影响。

感谢每一位曾经为 MindSpore 后端贡献代码与反馈问题的开发者。

items.title: [RFC]: Support ViT Full CUDA Graph (Tracker)
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation.

Multimodal large language models (e.g., Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5, GLM-V, Kimi K2.5) rely on a Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder to process visual inputs before feeding them into the language model backbone. In production serving scenarios, the ViT forward pass involves launching a large number of small CUDA kernels — including patch embedding, layer normalization, multi-head self-attention, and MLP projections — each of which incurs non-trivial kernel launch overhead on the host side.

Currently, vLLM supports CUDA graph capture for the decoder (LLM) portion of the model, which has proven effective at reducing kernel launch costs and improving throughput. However, the ViT encoder is still executed eagerly, meaning every forward pass re-launches all kernels from scratch. Extending full CUDA graph support to the ViT encoder would allow the entire encoder forward pass to be captured and replayed as a single graph, eliminating per-kernel launch overhead and enabling more consistent, low-latency inference for multimodal models.

items.title: [Bug]: CPU offload cannot pin regions of 512 GiB or more (single cudaHostRegister call)
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

GLM-5.2 on 4×H200 NVL, TP4/DCP4, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, vLLM `0.26.1rc1.dev255+g5e35a6f4f`, with CPU offload:

```
--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"block_size":256,"cpu_bytes_to_use":600000000000}}'
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`pin_mmap_region` registers the whole offload region with one `cudaHostRegister` call ([`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py:136`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py#L136)). A single registration of 512 GiB or more fails with `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` regardless of free memory, so any `cpu_bytes_to_use` at or above ~550e9 never gets pinned.

Bracketed with a standalone script (mmap in `/dev/shm` + `posix_fallocate` + `cudaHostRegister`), one process, 1.3 TB host RAM free, no model loaded:

| region size | result |
|---|---|
| 20 / 300 / 400 / 500 GB | success, ~0.1 s per GB |
| 549.0e9 (511.29 GiB) | success, 55.3 s |
| 549.7e9 (511.96 GiB) | success, 55.4 s |
| 549.9e9 (512.15 GiB) | **fails, code=2** |
| 551e9 / 600e9 | fails, code=2 |

So the ceiling is 512 GiB = 549,755,813,888 bytes per call. Rank count is irrelevant — one process reproduces it with 809 GB still available. I could not find this documented; NVIDIA forum reports mention other, lower ceilings in other setups (DAX-mapped memory, older drivers), so treating any single large registration as safe looks wrong in general.

This became reachable with #50094: before it each rank pinned its own `cpu_bytes_to_use / world_size` buffer (150 GB here) through torch's pinned allocator, all far below the ceiling; after it one shared region is registered in full by every rank.

items.title: [Bug][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer overwrites its own KV cache: backend advertises a kernel block size the kernels do not use
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

On ROCm, the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool sparse indexer **silently overwrites its own KV cache**. 4096 pool entries are written into 864 distinct slots, so ~79 % of the indexer's keys are wrong. The model still produces fluent text, so nothing crashes — long-context recall just degrades, and `temperature=0` stops being reproducible because the damage depends on which physical blocks the allocator hands out.

This is **ROCm-only** and distinct from #40018 (whose fix, #43781, is present in the tree I tested).

### Root cause

`DeepseekV32IndexerBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`):

```python
return [1, MultipleOf(16)] if current_platform.is_rocm() else [64]
```

On CUDA the backend declares exactly `[64]`, so vLLM sets `kernel_block_size = 64`, `BlockTable.use_hybrid_blocks = True`, and builds a kernel-granular block table. On ROCm it declares "any multiple of 16", so the hybrid aligner's choice (640 tokens here) is taken as natively supported: `blocks_per_kv_block == 1`, **no kernel-granular block table**.

But the kernels do not read 640-token blocks. DeepGEMM/AITER paged-MQA reads pool pages of 32 states; with `tokens_per_state == index_kpool == 4` that is 128 tokens. So the storage block (640 tok = 160 states) is five pages, and both `slot_mapping` and `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache_triton` address it with the **page** size (32) while the block table holds **spec-block** ids — a 5x over-subscription.

The intended split is even documented in `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/attention.py` as `storage_kernel_block_size`, but that identifier appears nowhere else in the tree — it was never implemented.

|---|---|---|

### Regression 1: `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` missing `record_logical_topk_ready`

```

    self.mla_attn.impl.record_logical_topk_ready()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
AttributeError: 'ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl' object has no attribute 'record_logical_topk_ready'
```

`mla.py:235` calls the new `record_logical_topk_ready()` API (defined on the base sparse impl in `sparse_mla_attention.py:717`), but `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py:756`) doesn't implement or inherit it. Engine dies at first forward.

Workaround: add a no-op `record_logical_topk_ready` to `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl`.

### Regression 2: JIT kernel warmup crash — `'function' object has no attribute 'compile'`

```
File "vllm/model_executor/warmup/jit_warmup_tilelang_helper.py", line 141, in launch
    compiled = jit_impl.compile(*args, **kwargs)
AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'compile'
```

The new `--kernel-config` jit-warmup subsystem (on by default, `enable_jit_warmup: bool = True`) crashes in the tilelang helper on this path. All 8 workers die at `JIT kernel warmup starting`.

Workaround: `--kernel-config '{"enable_jit_warmup": false}'`.

With both workarounds the model boots and serves (and for us it also carried the `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` fix for the 16K-chunk fault in #57227). Both regressions block any GLM-5.3-Flash ROCm serving on the nightly.

### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Motivation

We operate a production vLLM deployment (GLM-based MoE model, TP=4, 4x NVIDIA B200,
V1 engine) serving a workload dominated by very long prompts (RAG/long-context,
median ~100k-180k prompt tokens per request, generation typically <1k tokens).
Under this workload we consistently observe severe TTFT tail latency caused by
head-of-line blocking in prefill scheduling, and we believe this is a strong
real-world case for reviving #49075 / #55256.

## Problem

With `--enable-chunked-prefill` and `--max-num-batched-tokens` set to a
reasonably high value (tested 8192 and 16384), a single long-prompt request
still needs many scheduler iterations to complete its prefill
(prompt_tokens / max_num_batched_tokens ≈ 7-12 iterations for our 100k-180k

on an earlier vLLM version (`NotImplementedError: Concurrent Partial Prefill
is not supported`) with no maintainer response since April 2026. #49075
attempts to restore and properly enforce these fields in the V1 scheduler but
is currently open, unrebased, has an unresolved CodeRabbit finding on the
WAITING-loop admission check, and has never had CI run. #55256 proposed a

## [Bug][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash fails to boot on v0.29.1rc0 nightly: SparseAttnIndexerKpool (AMD) missing forward_cuda → NotImplementedError

### Current behavior

Serving GLM-5.3-Flash on the latest ROCm nightly (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-0bfc7a15d`, `vv0.29.1rc0.dev265+g0bfc7a15d`) crashes at `profile_run` on every worker rank:

```
(APIServer ... ) RuntimeError: Worker failed with error ''ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl' object has no attribute 'record_logical_topk_ready''

and, with that patched, the next blocker is:

```

    return self.forward_cuda(*args, **kwargs)

File "vllm/model_executor/custom_op.py", line 145, in forward_cuda
    raise NotImplementedError
NotImplementedError
```

### Root cause

`CustomOp.dispatch_forward` routes **enabled** ops to `forward_hip` on ROCm, and `forward_hip` falls back to `forward_cuda`. On this nightly the resolved `compilation_config.custom_ops` contains `'all'` (seen in the engine init log), which enables every registered op and triggers this deterministically.

The NVIDIA implementation (`nvidia/sparse_indexer.py`) defines both `forward_native` and `forward_cuda`; the AMD one is missing the alias the ROCm dispatch requires.

Alias at class level:

```python

```

(or define `forward_cuda` as a method calling `forward_native`), mirroring the NVIDIA implementation.

Some freezes clear after a few seconds. Some never clear. When a freeze does not clear, the engine dies and no worker writes an error. There is no traceback, no HIP error, no memory access fault and no watchdog message.

| Fatal engine deaths | 4 in 6 days |

items.bodyExcerpt:
Port [ROCm/ATOM#788](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/pull/788)'s indexer fused-kernel shape into vLLM. Replaces the `k_norm → rotary_emb → per_token_group_quant_fp8 → cache` chain (and the Q-side `per_token_group_quant_fp8`) inside `Indexer.forward` with a single AITER kernel `aiter.indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache` (ROCm/aiter#3185, correctness fixes in ROCm/aiter#3451).

> **Companion:** ROCm/aiter#3451 — required. Without it GSM8K strict-match drops 0.95 → 0.49.

## Gating

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_DSV32_INDEXER_FUSION` (default off) + main AITER toggle; auto-disabled when the running AITER build does not expose `indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache`. The kernel hard-asserts `index_head_dim == 128`, `qk_rope_head_dim == 64`, `head_dim == quant_block_size`; `Indexer.__init__` only enables the path if all three hold and `model_type != "glm_moe_dsa"`.

## Design notes

- **Stays inside the existing custom op.** Calling the fused kernel from inside `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer` keeps `q_fp8` and `weights_out` from escaping — an earlier version that registered them as a separate op leaked pointers across piecewise-cudagraph segments and tanked GSM8K to ~1%.
- **Persistent workspace** for `q_fp8` / `weights_out`, grown monotonically. Otherwise 61 indexer layers × 2 allocations per decode step churn the eager allocator.
- **K stride fixup.** The kernel asserts `k.stride(0) == head_dim`, but the upstream `.contiguous()` is a no-op on `size(0) == 1` views. We rewrite the metadata via `as_strided` when it's safe, else `empty + copy_`.
- **`preshuffle=True`.** Downstream consumers read MFMA 16×16 SHUFFLE; the original call site passed `False` and silently produced garbage. Bytewise-equal to the unfused triton write after the fix.
- **fp32 LN params** passed through as-is (required by ROCm/aiter#3451).

The vendored fallback LMCache connector (`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/lmcache_integration/multi_process_adapter.py`) was stale relative to the current `lmcache` package API:

1. **`IPCCacheEngineKey` → `IPCCacheServerKey`**: The key class was renamed in the LMCache codebase. The vendored connector still imported the old name, which would cause `ImportError` if the fallback path were ever reached.

items.title: [Bugfix] glm47 parser: tolerate missing opening <arg_value> tag
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

FIX #49248

Under concurrent load, GLM-4.7-family models sporadically skip the opening `<arg_value>` tag when emitting tool calls, producing

```
<tool_call>search<arg_key>query</arg_key>how many vacation days left</arg_value></tool_call>
```

with the argument value fully intact (raw sampled tokens captured via `logprobs: true`; reproduces at `temperature: 0` too, ~5–17% of calls at concurrency 6 on our production trace family, 0 sequentially).

`_ARG_RE`/`_PARTIAL_ARG_RE` in `vllm/parser/glm47_moe.py` require the opening tag, so such calls silently parse to `arguments: "{}"`, which then fails the client's tool schema validation and degrades agent loops (the broken `{}` call gets rendered back into history, so retries tend to fail the same way).

This PR makes the opening `<arg_value>` optional in both regexes. The closing `</arg_value>` still delimits the value, so:
- well-formed output parses exactly as before (the optional group matches the tag when present);
- streaming is unaffected: the incremental lexer buffers ambiguous tag prefixes, so a partially streamed `<arg_value>` never leaks into a value snapshot.

## Test Plan

- `tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py`: new non-streaming cases (single arg with missing opening tag; mixed malformed + well-formed args in one call) and a streaming case with the malformed sequence split across chunks; all pre-existing cases unchanged.
- Live validation on a 4×GPU GLM-5.2 deployment (`--tool-call-parser glm47`), replaying the production request that triggers the malformation at concurrency 6 with `logprobs: true`:
  - before: 12/120 responses parsed to `arguments: "{}"`;
  - after: 12/72 responses still show the raw malformation in sampled tokens (model-side quirk, expected), **all 12 parse to full arguments**, 0 empty; streaming replay 0/72 empty.

## Test Result

`pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py` — 16 passed.

items.bodyExcerpt:
Fixes #29945

## The bug

With MTP or any other in-checkpoint drafter, startup prints two different max
model lengths for the same run:

```
[model.py:554] Resolved architecture: Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration
[model.py:1684] Using max model len 131072
[model.py:554] Resolved architecture: Qwen3_5MTP
[model.py:1684] Using max model len 262144
```

Users read the second line as the drafter being sized for a longer context than
the target and reasonably conclude that KV cache is being over-allocated. The
issue has collected repeat reports on Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5 and GLM-4.5-Air since
December, including cases where an explicit `--max-model-len 8192` still printed
`Using max model len 262144` for the draft.

@benchislett investigated twice and confirmed there is no over-allocation, since
`SpeculativeConfig._maybe_override_draft_max_model_len` clamps the draft to the
target immediately after the model config is built, and invited a PR to fix the
log.

## Root cause

`ModelConfig` for the draft is constructed with
`spec_target_max_model_len=target_model_config.max_model_len`, but
`_get_and_verify_max_len` only consults that argument inside the
`derived_max_model_len == inf` branch, which is the fallback for checkpoints
that declare no length key at all. Every real MTP or EAGLE checkpoint does
declare one, so the argument is dead in practice and the draft resolves to its
own declared length, logs it, and is only corrected one step later by the
clamp in `SpeculativeConfig`.

So the bound exists twice, in two different places, and the value that gets
logged is the one from before the bound is applied.

Apply `spec_target_max_model_len` as an upper bound in `_get_and_verify_max_len`
whenever the length is being derived, so the draft resolves and logs the value
it will actually run with. The later clamp in `SpeculativeConfig` becomes a
no-op, which also stops its `Overriding draft model max model len` line from
firing on a config that was never wrong.

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM` and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM` both default to `True`. Once `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` is set, MLA `kv_b_proj` weights are re-quantized online regardless of the precision the checkpoint asked for, and there is no per-model opt-out.

- #48051 measures ~11% error per attention layer from this path, accumulating into repetition loops.
- On `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`, MTP acceptance rate goes 0% -> 58.5% when the re-quantization is skipped (#52833).

items.title: [Spec Decode] Support PCP-sharded MTP prefill
items.bodyExcerpt:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

Related RFC: #25749

Add single-module MTP support to the MRV2 PCP path while preserving PCP's long-prefill scaling:

- keep both the target prefill and the first MTP draft pass PCP-sharded
- restore target and draft outputs to global sequence order only at their sampling boundaries
- run later MTP proposal steps as replicated decode queries
- support pure prefill, replicated decode, mixed prefill/decode, and scheduled draft-token verification batches
- preserve GPU-materialized token positions after speculative rejection instead of rebuilding them from a potentially stale CPU cursor
- reuse the PCP manager's consumed rank-local input buffer and target hidden states for draft prefill, avoiding a doubled request buffer, metadata copies, and a redundant hidden-state all-gather
- scope rank-local state to the exact global batch so dummy/profile and stale batches use the ordinary global draft path
- distinguish PCP-expanded target slot mappings from ordinary replicated-draft mappings in sparse MLA
- disable MTP top-k index sharing under PCP and wait for proposal cache writes before a KV producer publishes the result
- account for PCP ranks in multi-node world-size and per-DP-rank placement
- reject unsupported multi-module MTP and CUDA-graph configurations during startup

This relies only on the PCP implementation already present on vLLM main and is independent of the fused PCP norm/RoPE work.

### Relationship to #53427

This is a materially different execution design from #53427. That PR keeps the target PCP-sharded but runs a fully replicated drafter on every PCP rank and currently excludes sparse MLA. This change shards the prompt-sized MTP draft pass across PCP ranks, supports the GLM-5.2 sparse-MLA path, and avoids repeating long-prefill draft compute and cache writes on every rank. It adopts the same GPU-cursor correctness principle for rank-local positions, but not the replicated-drafter architecture.

## Purpose

Two fixes to the `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` backend that are prerequisites for serving NoPE sparse-MLA models (`qk_rope_head_dim=0`, e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash / `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) with the `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache on SM120/SM121 devices such as the NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10). items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The read format has to match the write format. The vLLM writers used with this backend store each tile scale as raw fp32 amax / 448 (concat_and_cache_ds_mla and the DeepSeek-V3.2 fused Triton path). However, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` asked FlashInfer for `pow2_fp32`, which extracts the exponent and reconstructs `2^floor(log2(scale))`. For a non-power-of-two scale written by vLLM, that is smaller by a factor in `(0.5, 1]`.

The format was chosen from a `model_type` allowlist that only sent `glm*` to the correct reader, so every other sparse model landing here reads its scales wrong: DeepSeek-V3.2 today, and HY V4 as soon as it can select this backend (it needs
the sink support in the stacked follow-up, since `learnable_sink` defaults to on). https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54434

FlashInfer supports both scale conventions for the same 656-byte physical layout, but vLLM's writer contract currently always stores arbitrary fp32 scales. Kimi-K3 demonstrates that this convention is not tied to the model label: its dense MLA path writes the same layout even though it never reaches this sparse backend. This backend accepts no other layout (it raises unless
`kv_cache_dtype == "fp8_ds_mla"`), so its reader format becomes a constant.

DeepSeek-V4 is not a counterexample. It reuses the `fp8_ds_mla` string for a different footer-scale layout: 576 bytes of per-token data plus 8 bytes of UE8M0 `2^(u8-127)` scales in the page footer, or 584 logical bytes per token.
That layout is written by DSv4's own CuteDSL/Triton insert rather than `concat_and_cache_ds_mla`, and DSv4 is rejected here: `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` is not a DSv4 backend; those models must use `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`.

items.title: [Bugfix][Parser] GLM-4.7: stray arg tags must not leak into tool-call argument keys
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes a tool-call corruption in the GLM-4.7 parser: stray `arg_key` markup leaks into the parsed argument **key**, so the client rejects the call.

Observed in production against a GLM server run with `--tool-call-parser glm47`:

```
list_dir({"path</arg_key>": "/Users/user/Desktop/project"})
-> client error: "must have required property 'path'"
```

The client rejects the call, the agent loses the step, and the model retries with an invented path.

**Root cause.** `_glm47_arg_converter` matched the key with an unbounded non-greedy group:

```python
r"<arg_key>(?P<key>.*?)</arg_key>\s*<arg_value>(?P<value>.*?)</arg_value>"
```

`.*?` is non-greedy but it is *not* bounded by the delimiter it is scanning for. If the stream contains a repeated or stray `arg_key` tag, the engine backtracks past the first `</arg_key>` because that is what it takes to reach the following `<arg_value>`, and the extra markup ends up inside the key. On

```
<arg_key>path</arg_key></arg_key><arg_value>/tmp/x</arg_value>
```

the old code yields `{"path</arg_key>": "/tmp/x"}`, reproducing the observed string exactly. The mirrored `<arg_key><arg_key>path…` case yields `{"<arg_key>path": "/tmp/x"}`.

**Fix.** Match runs of non-`<` text so the key group cannot cross its own delimiter, and accept a run of closing tags so a duplicate is skipped rather than shifting the key:

```python
_ARG_KEY = r"<arg_key>(?P<key>[^<]*+(?:<(?!/?arg_key>)[^<]*+)*+)(?:</arg_key>\s*)+"
```

Both `_ARG_RE` and `_PARTIAL_ARG_RE` are built from it, so the streaming path gets the same guarantee.

The unrolled possessive form is deliberate rather than the simpler tempered dot `(?:(?!</?arg_key>).)*`. `_compute_arg_delta` re-runs the converter over the whole accumulated buffer on every argument chunk, so the common streaming case is a *failing* match against a partial buffer — precisely where a tempered dot backtracks per character. items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][ROCm] Fix MoRI-IO KV block-offset for speculative decoding (MTP)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary
`compute_block_transfer_offsets` in the MoRI-IO KV connector raised `ValueError: local_block_ids longer than remote_block_ids` whenever the producer's local block count exceeded the consumer's. Under **speculative decoding (e.g. MTP)** with `block_size=1`, the prefill (producer) KV-cache manager reserves `num_speculative_tokens` lookahead slots that the decode (consumer) side does not allocate, so `local` exceeds `remote` by exactly the spec-token count (e.g. **8003 vs 8000** at n=3). This crashed the first prefill→decode KV write and made MTP unusable over MoRI-IO PD-disaggregation.

## Fix
Block order is positional (`block_size=1`), so the prompt KV is the prefix and the extra local blocks are empty lookahead scratch. Clamp `local_block_ids` to `local[:len(remote)]` and transfer only the prompt prefix — symmetric with the existing shorter-local handling already documented in the same function.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Problem

Ordinary V3.2 sparse MLA and its indexer can resolve to `BLHNC` even when the packed block stride is not a whole number of every segment's physical rows. Binding/warmup then asserts; sparse row indexing requires the same invariant. This addresses the ordinary native-64-row allocation problem in #55431 and the geometry prerequisite discussed in #55434.

## Root cause

The allocator sums logical page bytes without encoding sparse consumers' row-addressing requirements. Physical rows include format metadata: 656 bytes for DS-FP8, 352 for DS-NVFP4, and 132 for the FP8 indexer. A heterogeneous sum need not divide by each row width.

## Fix

Declare `MLAAttentionSpec.block_stride_alignment_bytes` from the physical row widths and align the total packed block stride to their LCM. Carry that stride through allocation, capacity checks, overrides, auto-fit, and PP re-planning; merge requirements by LCM.

Preserve logical page sizes, integer-row index units, and layer-compact behavior. Declare BLHNC alongside existing supported layer-compact layouts; retain rejection of other unvalidated block-outermost layouts and unsupported manager/kernel splitting. No kernel, NIXL, or OffloadingConnector implementation changes.

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Cap glm5next video sampling knobs
items.bodyExcerpt:
Fixes #55726

## Purpose

`glm_sample_frame_indices` walks `duration * target_fps` candidates and
deduplicates only at the end, so `Glm5NextVideoBackend` sizes that walk from the
requested fps rather than from the clip. On a 2-frame, 1-second source it spends
857 ms and 156 MiB to return 2 indices.

This clamps `target.fps` to `source.original_fps`. No sampling rate above the
source rate can return frames the container does not hold, so the walk becomes
bounded by the frame count while the sampled indices stay identical.

## Why not a fixed ceiling

An earlier revision copied GLMGA's `_MAX_FPS = 30` / `_MAX_FRAMES = 2048`. As
@JaredforReal pointed out, that ceiling has no basis in the GLM-5.3-Flash video
processor: its `processor_config.json` sets only `fps: 2` as the default
interval. A fixed 30 would also halve sampling for a legitimate 60 fps request.

Clamping to the source rate needs no magic number, and it makes the `max_frames`
ceiling unnecessary: with fps bounded, `extract_t` cannot exceed the frame count,
so `max_frames=100_000` keeps returning 10_000 indices exactly as on main.

## Measurements

Serving image, calling the backend directly, 2-frame 1-second clip, `fps` and
`max_frames` set to the same value:

| requested | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 200 000 | 11.9 ms, +1 MiB | 3.1 ms, +0 MiB |
| 2 000 000 | 87.4 ms, +18 MiB | 0.0 ms, +0 MiB |
| 20 000 000 | 857.5 ms, +156 MiB | 0.0 ms, +0 MiB |

Output is unchanged in every case: 2 indices for the 2-frame source, 900 for a
900-frame 30 fps clip, 2048 for a 10 000-frame one, and the default interval
still yields the same 60 indices as the bare sampler.

items.title: [Bugfix][Parser] Poolside: stray arg_key tags must not leak into tool-call argument keys
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`PoolsideV1ToolParser.func_arg_regex` captures the argument key with a plain
`.*?`:

```python
self.func_arg_regex = re.compile(
    r"<arg_key>(.*?)</arg_key>\s*<arg_value>(.*?)</arg_value>", re.DOTALL
)
```

A non-greedy `.*?` guarantees only the *shortest match consistent with the
rest of the pattern*, not that it stops at the first literal `</arg_key>`.
If `\s*<arg_value>` fails to match right after that first occurrence, the
engine backtracks and lets `.*?` cross the boundary to reach a *later*
`</arg_key>`, silently absorbing a stray `<arg_key>`/`</arg_key>` tag into
the parsed key.

This is the identical defect class and identical fix shape as the GLM-4.7
leak fixed in #54971 (reviewer Manny7717 flagged this exact call site in
that PR's review, at `vllm/tool_parsers/poolside_v1_tool_parser.py:82`).
The fix bounds the key to runs of non-`<` text, so the capture group can
never cross its own delimiter:

```python
self.func_arg_regex = re.compile(
    r"<arg_key>([^<]*+(?:<(?!/?arg_key>)[^<]*+)*+)(?:</arg_key>\s*)+"
    r"<arg_value>(.*?)</arg_value>",
    re.DOTALL,
)
```

This file uses the third-party `regex` module (`import regex as re`), not
stdlib `re` — `regex` has always supported possessive quantifiers (`*+`)
regardless of interpreter version, so (unlike a stdlib-`re` site) no
non-possessive fallback is needed here. The repo's `requires-python` floor
is `>=3.10,<3.15`; the dev venv used for testing runs 3.13.15, and a
20,000-case randomized differential check (see Test Result) against the
old pattern found no divergence on well-formed input and no leaked `<` in
malformed input.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55087.

GLM-5.3 KDA lazily merges the q/k/v convolution weights into a single cached tensor for the fused causal-conv path. During online RL or refit workflows, the underlying q/k/v convolution weights can be updated after warmup, but the derived merged tensor may remain stale. Subsequent inference can then continue using old or dummy weights even after the model weights have been refreshed.

This change:

- adds explicit invalidation for the merged KDA convolution-weight cache
- invalidates the KDA cache before GLM-5.3 model weight loading
- covers both the direct model-loading path and the top-level CausalLM loading path
- keeps the merged-weight cache for normal inference when weights are unchanged
- retains version/storage checks as additional protection against direct tensor mutations
- preserves the hot-path behavior by rebuilding only when needed

This PR is a follow-up to #53906, which introduced the GLM-5.3 implementation.

## Root cause

The KDA layer builds a single merged q|k|v convolution weight tensor and caches it in `_merged_conv_weight`. That cache was not always invalidated when the source q/k/v conv weights were replaced. In online-RL refit/update flows, this allowed stale merged weights to persist across reloads and be reused in later inference steps.

## Fix

- add invalidate_merged_conv_weight() / invalidate_kda_conv_weight_caches() methods to manually clear the stale cache
- invoke invalidation before every load_weights() call so refits always rebuild from fresh weights
- add explicit invalidation hooks for the merged KDA cache

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Skip non-prefix-cacheable groups in SimpleCPUOffload (GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail and QSA)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash carries a kpool-tail scratch group (`KpoolTailSpec`, `prefix_cacheable=False`, `block_size=index_kpool=4`) next to prefix-cacheable groups that hash at 1152 tokens on this box (MLA 1152, 4× Mamba 1152 in `align` mode). Core (`resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes`, `HybridKVCacheCoordinator`, `KVCacheManager`) and the `MooncakeStore connector` already skip such groups. `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` did not, and treated every KV cache group as offloadable:

- `_select_eager_blocks_to_store` views the request hashes at each group's block size to build `BlockStored` metadata. For the tail group that is `resolve_block_hashes(hashes, hash_block_size=1152, block_size=4)`, which trips the divisibility assert as soon as `--kv-events-config` enables KV cache events. The engine dies on the first prefill store.
- `update_state_after_alloc` maps external (CPU-hit) tokens onto the scratch group and asserts alignment against its block size, although the coordinator never returns hit blocks for it.

This PR records which groups take part in offloading (`prefix_cacheable`) and skips the rest in eager store selection and in load pairing. Scratch blocks never carry a hash, so nothing is stored or loaded for them either way; the scratch slot in the per-group hit tuple stays empty, exactly as the coordinator leaves it.


## Duplication check

Two open PRs touch the same code path: #55033 (draft since 2026-09-02, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA ring, also adjusts `_estimate_lazy_target_blocks`) and #56404 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, gates `resolve_block_hashes` in the store path only, currently conflicting). This PR is scoped to the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool-tail layout and adds what neither of them covers: a regression test for the actual crash trigger (`enable_kv_cache_events=true`, `BlockStored` emitted for cacheable groups only) and an end-to-end store/load + accuracy check on GLM-5.3-Flash. Happy to fold the test into #55033 instead if the maintainers prefer to land that one.

items.title: [KVConnector][NIXL] Opt-in per-layer overlapped WRITE-push for disaggregated KV transfer
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary / motivation

The stock `NixlConnector` transfers KV as a single, monolithic READ at the end of
prefill, so KV transfer does **not** overlap with prefill compute. On
disaggregated (P/D-split) inference this leaves throughput on the table versus
push-style transports.

This PR adds an **opt-in, per-layer overlapped WRITE-push** path: the prefill
side pushes each layer's KV to the decode worker as soon as that layer is
computed, overlapping KV transfer with the tail of prefill and closing the
throughput gap against push-style connectors — while staying on the open,
standard UCX/NIXL path.

Design notes / rationale live in the commit message and inline docstrings in
`push_worker.py` (module docstring describes the event-driven push pipeline).

## Design

- **Per-layer save hook** (`save_kv_layer`): records a CUDA event per layer and
  enqueues **one RDMA WRITE per KV region off-thread**, so the forward thread is
  never blocked on transfer.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Release obsolete FlashMLA scratch storage when another layer grows the shared workspace.

`FlashMLASparseImpl` keeps constructor-time tensor views in `q_concat_buffer`, `prefill_bf16_workspace`, and, with PCP+DCP, `gathered_kv_workspace`. When `WorkspaceManager` grows its allocation, those views keep the old storage alive. Both buffers remain allocated, reducing the memory available for KV cache.

This change stores shapes and dtypes, reserves capacity during initialization, and reacquires simultaneous views from the current workspace when used. Workspace sizing, tensor layout, and the manager's locking policy remain unchanged.

### Observed impact

We reproduced this on GLM-5.3 with DP/EP64, TP1, MTP1, automatic KV/context sizing, and a 0.95 GPU memory target, using a vLLM 0.29.0-based deployment. Allocator snapshots showed a 5,904 MiB FlashMLA workspace retained alongside a new 6,144 MiB MoE workspace on 18 of 64 ranks. The new allocation was traced to `FusedMoEKernelModularImpl._allocate_buffers` during profiling.

The corresponding fix on that deployed version produced these startup measurements:

| Measurement | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ranks retaining both allocations | 18 | 0 |
| Minimum KV capacity per rank | 490,816 tokens | 603,904 tokens |
| Total KV capacity across 64 ranks | 36,934,975 tokens | 38,971,455 tokens |

Total allocated memory recovered was **103.78125 GiB**. These are startup allocation measurements, not throughput or model-accuracy results. This PR ports the fix to current upstream and also covers its PCP+DCP gather buffer.

Searched open PRs for `flashmla workspace` and `workspace memory leak`, and checked issue #51743 and its linked open PRs. ## Summary

- route rope-free sparse MLA to the ROCm Triton implementation for every KV-cache dtype

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Required to run GLM-5.3-Flash on MI350, otherwise errors during warmup with:

```bash
File "vllm/model_executor/warmup/jit_warmup.py", line 969, in compile_many
  self.compile(compile_key)
File "vllm/model_executor/warmup/jit_warmup_tilelang_helper.py", line 141, in launch
  return compile_tilelang(jit_impl, *args, **call_kwargs)
File "vllm/model_executor/warmup/jit_warmup_tilelang_helper.py", line 104, in compile_tilelang
  compiled = jit_impl.compile(*args, **kwargs)
AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'compile'
```

### Why

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51159 added lazy import of tilelang and made the `tilelang_jit` decorator return a **regular function on ROCm** instead of a `tilelang.jit.JITImpl`. On ROCm, this function would create and return the JITImpl when **called**. That's fine as long as you just _call_ the kernel the first time you need it, which is how warmup was previously done.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50178 refactored the warmup logic of tilelang mHC kernels. Previously the warmup was done by literally calling/running the mHC layers. After that PR, warmup now runs `.compile(...)` on the kernel to compile it, and later caches the compiled kernel manually. That's ok on CUDA where the kernel is a JITImpl, but not on ROCm where it's a regular function.

Hence the assumption that the tilelang kernel will be _called_ the first time it's used is no longer true. It's no longer launched during warmup, just `.compiled()`. This PR ensures that the first time we touch the (lazily created) kernel we convert it into a JITImpl to be compiled.

## Why this is not duplicating #56604

#56604 (open since 2026-09-12) fixes the same crash class by adding a **default no-op `record_logical_topk_ready` on the `MLAAttentionImpl` base class** in `vllm/v1/attention/backend.py`, so every backend silently inherits it.

This PR instead adds the method **on `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` itself**, mirroring the existing `SparseMLACommonImpl` contract (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/sparse_mla_attention.py:717`): impls that participate in sparse-MLA index groups implement the hook with real semantics; impls that don't declare an explicit no-op at their own site.

Trade-off: the base-class default in #56604 is broader (also covers any other backend that skips `SparseMLACommonImpl`) but weakens the interface — a new sparse backend that *should* implement index-group notification would silently no-op instead of failing loudly. This PR keeps that failure loud and fixes the one backend that currently crashes (ROCm AITER sparse MLA, GLM-5.3-Flash on MI350X). Either fix resolves the boot regression in #57248; happy to withdraw this in favor of #56604 if maintainers prefer the base-class default.

`MLAAttention.forward` calls `impl.record_logical_topk_ready()` on every sparse layer (`vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py:235`). `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` inherits `SharedTopkIndicesBuffer` directly (not `SparseMLACommonImpl`) and never gained the method, so serving GLM-5.3-Flash on ROCm (gfx950, `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`) crashes at the first forward with `AttributeError: 'ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl' object has no attribute 'record_logical_topk_ready'`.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Cache][GLM-5.3-Flash] Disable slot mapping kernel for the kpool tail buffer
items.bodyExcerpt:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57227.

GLM-5.3-Flash crashes with MAF when sending 500k ISL prompts.  This is caused by out of bounds indexing in the default `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` applied to the Kpool tail buffer. The kpool tail buffer has a fixed size for each request and anyway uses its own slot mapping kernel `compute_kpool_tail_slot_mapping`, and hence should not use the default kernel.

**Alternatively: make KpoolTailSpec inherit from CircularBufferSpec instead of the SW spec.**

## Why

The KpoolTailSpec is a ring buffer with one block per requests, and is addressed by `pos % kpool` (bounded). The generic slot mapping kernel `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` addresses by `pos // kernel_block_size` (unbounded), and it's used to be enabled for all kv specs except for `CircularBufferSpec`. 

#53781 refactored what kv specs should use this generic slot mapping kernel to instead those specs declaring `uses_slot_mapping: true`. However, KpoolTailSpec inherits from SW and not the circular buffer spec, meaning it still deemed to use the generic slot mapping kernel even though it's a ring buffer. Since that kernels addressing grows unbounded with sequence length (`pos // kernel_block_size`) while the actual KpoolTail buffer is fixed in size, this eventually triggered a MAF at long enough requests.

This PR fixes is it by excluding not using this generic slot mapping kernel for KpoolTailSpec. Instead it just relies on its tailored `compute_kpool_tail_slot_mapping` inside the metadata builder.

items.title: WIP: fix(decode bench): remember zero-token prefix fills
items.bodyExcerpt:
DecodeBenchConnector currently records a request as filled only when the
  synthetic prefill contains at least one external token. A one-token prompt has
  a zero-token synthetic prefill, so a later preemption causes the connector to
  treat generated output as a new prompt and offer it as externally computed KV.

  With HiSparse, that false import can reach the host-only path at an arbitrary
  token offset and terminate the engine with:

  ValueError: A host-only HiSparse import must end on a cache-block boundary.

  This change records the completed one-shot lookup after allocation, even when
  the external token count is zero. This prevents generated history from being
  refilled after preemption while preserving retries after failed allocation.

  The reproduction used a two-node GLM-5.2-FP8 EP16 decode deployment with
  DecodeBenchConnector composed with HiSparseConnector, one input token, 10,624
  requested output tokens, and 128 fixed requests per GPU. The failure occurred
  when GPU KV pressure first caused requests to be preempted and readmitted.

## Purpose

Fixes #57424. `SparseAttnIndexerKpool` on the AMD/ROCm path (`vllm/models/glm5next/amd/sparse_indexer.py`) defines only `forward_native`. `CustomOp.dispatch_forward` routes *enabled* ops to `forward_hip` on ROCm, and `forward_hip` falls back to `forward_cuda` — which doesn't exist → `NotImplementedError` at the first forward of the indexer op.

On the `v0.29.1rc0.dev265+g0bfc7a15d` ROCm nightly, serving GLM-5.3-Flash crashes at `profile_run` with:

File "vllm/model_executor/custom_op.py", line 149, in forward_hip
    return self.forward_cuda(*args, **kwargs)
File "vllm/model_executor/custom_op.py", line 145, in forward_cuda
    raise NotImplementedError

The NVIDIA `SparseAttnIndexerKpool` defines both `forward_native` and `forward_cuda`; the AMD one is native-only but was never given the alias the ROCm dispatch requires. This blocks GLM-5.3-Flash boot on current ROCm nightlies entirely.

items.bodyExcerpt:
Reviving #55256's clean threshold-independent `max_concurrent_prefills` limit for the V1 scheduler to fix the exact head-of-line blocking issue reported in #57413.

items.title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Address kpool tail blocks by the padded indexer stride in the NVIDIA prefill seed kernel
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix silent indexer-cache corruption for GLM-5.3-Flash on NVIDIA: the kpool prefill tail-seed kernel addresses tail blocks with a dense stride while the tail cache is stored with the indexer's padded block stride.

**How the tail cache is laid out.** `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` pads the `KpoolTailSpec` page to the indexer page (`page_size_padded = idx_page`; 38016 B for the default `block_size=1152`: 288 pool rows x 132 B), and `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` places every indexer layer's tail tensor at the *same offset* as that layer's indexer tensor with `block_stride = idx_page`. Tail block `b` is therefore the first 2048 B (`[2, kpool=4, 128]` bf16) of indexer block `b`; the two never collide because both groups draw distinct block ids from one pool. `create_kv_cache_views` builds the view with `as_strided`, so `tail_kv_cache.stride(0) == 19008` elements instead of the dense 1024.

**The bug.** `_kpool_tail_seed_kernel` in `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/kpool_compress.py` computed

```python
base = (blk * 2 * KPOOL + t % KPOOL) * HEAD_DIM   # dense 2048 B block stride
```

so for every prefill it (a) left the request's own tail block unseeded and (b) wrote 2048 B of raw bf16 K / gate rows at byte `blk * 2048` of the layer's indexer region, i.e. into indexer block `blk * 2048 // 38016` at offset `blk * 2048 % 38016` — fp8 key rows or the fp32 scale region of whatever request owns that block. ## Purpose

Add tuned W8A8 block-FP8 triton GEMM configs for gfx950 (AMD Instinct MI350X, `device_name=0x75b0`). These cover the four MLA projection GEMM shapes exercised by GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`); the configs directory currently has zero entries for gfx950, so the kernel falls back to default tile configs with a "Performance might be sub-optimal!" warning at boot.

Shapes added (N, K): (3072, 4096), (4096, 1536), (4096, 256), (512, 4096) — each with 12 M buckets spanning decode (M=1..256) and prefill (M=1024..16384).

## Methodology

Swept triton launch configs (BLOCK_SIZE_M/N/K, GROUP_SIZE_M, num_warps, num_stages) per M bucket against `_w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` on MI350X (ROCm 7.2.3, vllm nightly 0bfc7a15d), `triton.testing.do_bench` timing, selecting the fastest valid config per bucket. JSONs follow the existing `get_w8a8_block_fp8_configs()` lookup format.

## Validation

Serving GLM-5.3-Flash on 8x MI350X (TP=8, breakable cudagraphs, aiter MoE/MLA), identical `vllm bench serve` runs before/after:

| Profile | Metric | default configs | tuned configs | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| in=2048 out=512 conc=32 | mean TTFT | 5214 ms | 3178 ms | -39% |
| in=2048 out=512 conc=32 | mean TPOT | 22.98 ms | 17.99 ms | -22% |
| in=32768 out=256 conc=8 | mean TTFT | 3385 ms | 2934 ms | -13% |
| in=32768 out=256 conc=8 | mean TPOT | 30.88 ms | 26.93 ms | -13% |

Boot log confirms all 32 "Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config" warnings replaced by "Using configuration from ..." lookups. Full correctness suite (mixed chunked-prefill/decode repro, 32K-524K long-context ladder) passes with zero memory-access faults.

N/A — data-only change (JSON config files); no code paths modified.
